haiku-low.q1: It returns the popular-items list (20 IDs) with fallback: true and reason timeout or no_features.
haiku-low.q2: It keeps using the last good records until they are 6 hours old, then treats features as missing and falls back to popular items.
haiku-low.q3: No. Shadow output is stored and compared, never shown. A shadow failure or dropped job does not affect the user's response.
haiku-low.q4: Users where hash(salt + user_id) mod 100 is under 10, the same fixed 10% for every candidate, excluding fallback responses.
haiku-low.q5: At least 7 days in shadow, error rate under 0.5%, p99 under 80 ms, live compatibility check passing, and ML lead approval recorded for that version and report.
haiku-low.q6: NOT STATED. The plan says product has not decided whether a live A/B test comes between shadow and the full switch.
haiku-low.q7: Every instance polls the active pointer every 10 seconds, loads the new version, smoke-tests it, and switches in memory. No redeploy.
haiku-low.q8: After responding, the API sends the feature vector from its own lookup in a shadow job. The worker does no lookup, and the job is non-blocking, so latency is unaffected.
haiku-low.q9: If the queue is full or unreachable, the job is dropped and a drop counter goes up. The user is unaffected.
haiku-low.q10: Each shadow job writes one row keyed by request ID with both outputs. A daily report compares the two 20-item lists for overlap; the ML lead interprets it.
haiku-low.q11: Registration and shadow start run a compatibility check against the store schema, and promotion repeats it. At runtime, records lacking required features fall back.
haiku-low.q12: An operator writes the active pointer back to the recorded previous version, which stays warm. Instances switch at the next 10-second poll, within 1 minute.

sonnet.q1: A popular-items list (20 IDs) with fallback: true and a reason (timeout or no_features); no model call is made.
sonnet.q2: It keeps serving the old records already in the store, until they are more than 6 hours old (now - as_of > 6h). After that those users get the fallback (stale_features). Alerts fire at 2h and 4h without success.
sonnet.q3: No. Shadow output is stored and compared, never shown to a user. Shadow failures cannot affect the user: queue full or unreachable drops the job and increments a drop counter, and any exception is caught and logged. The shadow job is queued after the response is sent.
sonnet.q4: Users with hash(salt + user_id) mod 100 < 10 (a fixed salt, so roughly 10%, always the same users), and only when the response was not a fallback.
sonnet.q5: It must be registered and shadowed, then pass the promotion gate: at least 7 days in shadow; error rate under 0.5%; p99 inference latency under 80 ms; the compatibility check passes again against the live store; and the ML lead's approval is recorded for this version number and the report they saw. Then the pointer is written with compare-and-set against the expected current version.
sonnet.q6: NOT DECIDED. Product has not decided whether an A/B test sits between shadow and the full switch. The plan chooses neither; if chosen, a new stage would go between steps 14 and 15.
sonnet.q7: Every instance polls the registry's active pointer (version number, change ID) every 10 seconds. On a new pointer it downloads and loads the artifact, runs a smoke inference on a fixed sample, then switches. The switch is a pointer change in the registry, with no redeploy. If loading fails, the instance keeps the old version and alerts.
sonnet.q8: The API puts the feature vector it already fetched in step 3 into the shadow job, so the worker does no feature lookup of its own. Shadow adds no latency because the job is queued after the response is sent, without blocking, and the queue and workers run outside the API on separate machines.
sonnet.q9: If the queue is full or unreachable, the job is dropped and a drop counter goes up. Drops are shown separately and never counted as passes. If the drop rate is high (for example over 5%) or volume is low, the report says the sample is not trustworthy. Drops should be watched in case they are not random. If a worker cannot write, the job is lost and counted as dropped.
sonnet.q10: In the shadow results store, one row per shadow job keyed by request ID. Each row holds request ID, user ID, candidate version and output, active version and output, latency and error or none. The comparison is a daily summary report on the candidate's registry record. The gate metrics are error rate, p99 latency, days in shadow and volume. The informational comparison is the overlap of the two 20-item lists and where they differ, with no quality threshold, and the ML lead decides what it means.
sonnet.q11: At shadow start, the registry compatibility check refuses the version if any manifest feature is missing from the store schema or not produced by the materialization job. The promotion gate rechecks it against the live store. At runtime, step 4 treats features as missing if the record lacks a required feature or the schema mismatches, so the request falls back (missing_feature) instead of running the model. A feature is also never removed while the active or previous version needs it. Shadow rows for users lacking a needed feature are skipped.
sonnet.q12: An operator action writes the active pointer back to the recorded previous version, which is still warm in each instance's memory, so no download is needed. Instances see it at the next 10-second poll, so it takes about 10 seconds, inside the 1-minute requirement. It needs no approval, and the reason is recorded. It depends on the registry being available.
